2607.28119.title: Challenges in annotations by humans and LLMs: A case study of evaluative language
2607.28119.paper_summary: In this paper, we draw a comparison between linguists in training, a trained linguist, and annotations generated by large language models (LLMs) to find out if they struggle with complex linguistic phenomena in a similar way. For this purpose, we analyse evaluative language in spoken popular science discourse, with the example of a corpus of English TED talk transcripts. We focus on the Appraisal theory and its Attitude subsystem, including the categories (classes) of Affect, Judgement, and Appreciation. In this context, Appraisal theory is an example of a highly subjective annotation task, making it a suitable example for the study of complex annotation challenges. First, we assess human annotations on a sentence level in specific scientific domains. Then, we develop three prompts and compare them for model performance for the automatic classification of Appraisal classes. We assess the performance of three LLMs using the best-performing prompt and finetune the model, reaching an F1-score of 0.77. We find that models perform best compared to annotations conducted by the trained linguist, while linguists in training do not reach high agreement scores. We conclude that LLMs can aid in complex annotation task resolution, opening new pathways for the complex theories annotated and analyzed in digital humanities studies.
2607.28119.paper_summary_zh: 在本文中，我們比較了正在訓練中的語言學家、受過訓練的語言學家以及大型語言模型（LLMs）生成的註釋，以了解他們在處理複雜語言現象時是否面臨相似的挑戰。為此，我們分析了口語流行科學話語中的評價性語言，以英語TED演講稿的語料庫為例。我們專注於評價理論及其態度子系統，包括情感、判斷和欣賞這三個類別（類別）。在這個背景下，評價理論是一個高度主觀的註釋任務的例子，使其成為研究複雜註釋挑戰的合適範例。首先，我們在特定的科學領域對人類註釋進行句子層級的評估。然後，我們開發了三個提示，並比較它們在自動分類評價類別方面的模型性能。我們使用表現最佳的提示評估三個LLMs的性能，並對模型進行微調，達到0.77的F1分數。我們發現，與受過訓練的語言學家進行的註釋相比，模型的表現最佳，而正在訓練中的語言學家則未能達到高一致性得分。我們得出結論，LLMs可以幫助解決複雜的註釋任務，為數位人文研究中標註和分析的複雜理論開辟新的途徑。
